pages.title: Admissions
pages.content:
Children aged 4 to 18 may enter in August or January, and at other times when a place is open. Applications are read on a rolling basis.

Who can apply

Kanade International School welcomes children aged 4 to 18, from Kindergarten through Grade 12. The school teaches in English and has 640 students from about 40 nationalities on one campus in Lisbon. Principal entry points are August and January. When a place is free at another point in the year, applications are read on a rolling basis. A child does not need to arrive already fluent in English. Lessons are in English, students keep a home language, and Portuguese begins in Kindergarten. Families who are new to the city and families already living here follow the same five steps. The first reply comes from the admissions office within two school days of an enquiry.

Five steps to a place

1. Enquire. Email admissions@kanade-school.example or call +351 21 000 4800. The office replies within two school days.

2. Visit. Come to an open morning, or ask for a private tour of the campus at Rua do Jardim Alto 18, 1400-150 Lisboa.

3. Apply online. Send previous school reports with the application and pay the application fee of €250. The fee is charged once and is non-refundable.

4. Assessment and family meeting. After the application is complete, both take place within ten school days.

5. Offer. The enrolment deposit of €2,000 confirms the place. It is charged once and credited to the final term.

Office hours for these conversations are Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 16:30.

Next open mornings

Open mornings are on Tuesdays from 9:30 to 11:00. The next three dates are Tuesday 10 November 2026, Tuesday 12 January 2027 and Tuesday 9 February 2027. Each morning is a walk through the campus with time for questions about entry, languages and the shape of the school day. Arrival for the school day itself is 8:20, lessons run from 8:30 to 15:20, and activities continue until 16:30. An open morning is shorter than a school day and is the usual way to visit before applying. A private tour is possible when these Tuesdays do not suit. Book through Leila Haddad, Director of Admissions, on the admissions email or on +351 21 000 4800. Places on each morning are held for families who have booked.

What to send with the application

A complete application has two things the school asks for at that step: previous school reports, and the application fee of €250. The fee is one-time and non-refundable. Reports let the school read the child’s recent schooling before the assessment and the family meeting, which follow within ten school days of a complete file. There is no separate document charge. Kindergarten applicants who have not yet attended school should say so in the enquiry, and the admissions office will explain what to send instead of reports. After an offer, the enrolment deposit of €2,000 confirms the place and is credited to the final term. Questions about the file go to admissions@kanade-school.example during office hours, Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 16:30.

Leila Haddad, Director of Admissions

Leila Haddad is Director of Admissions and the person families write to from the first enquiry through to the offer. She reads applications for Kindergarten to Grade 12, for August and January entry, and for rolling places when a space is open. Write to admissions@kanade-school.example or call +351 21 000 4800. The office is at Rua do Jardim Alto 18, 1400-150 Lisboa, Portugal, and is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 16:30. She can book a Tuesday open morning or a private tour, confirm whether a year group has room, and explain the application fee of €250 and the enrolment deposit of €2,000. A reply to a new enquiry is sent within two school days.

pages.title: Fees
pages.content:
Fees for 2026–27 are in euros per school year, and may be paid in three instalments. The eight charges below are the full list.

Fees for 2026–27

Fees are in euros for the 2026–27 school year, unless the line says the charge is one-time. They are payable in three instalments, in August, January and April. A family who pays the year in full by 15 July receives 3 percent off. From the third child onward, tuition is reduced by 10 percent. That reduction applies to tuition only.

Application fee (one-time, non-refundable): €250. Enrolment deposit (one-time, credited to the final term): €2,000. Kindergarten (ages 4–5): €14,800. Primary Years, Grades 1–5: €17,600. Middle Years, Grades 6–10: €20,400. Diploma Programme, Grades 11–12: €23,900. School bus (optional): €1,650. Lunch programme (optional): €1,280.

What tuition includes

Tuition for the year covers books, day trips, and IB exam registration for students in the Diploma Programme in Grades 11 and 12. Kindergarten is €14,800, Primary Years Grades 1–5 are €17,600, Middle Years Grades 6–10 are €20,400, and the Diploma Programme Grades 11–12 is €23,900. The school bus at €1,650 and the lunch programme at €1,280 are optional and are not part of tuition. The application fee of €250 and the enrolment deposit of €2,000 are separate one-time charges. The deposit is credited to the final term. Fees are for the 2026–27 school year and may be paid in three instalments, in August, January and April.

Instalments and the sibling reduction

The three instalment dates are August, January and April. Families who prefer to pay the school year in one amount, and who do so by 15 July, receive 3 percent off. The third child and every further child receives 10 percent off tuition. The 10 percent does not apply to the application fee of €250, the enrolment deposit of €2,000, the school bus at €1,650 or the lunch programme at €1,280. A family with children in different year groups pays the tuition set for each band: Kindergarten €14,800, Grades 1–5 €17,600, Grades 6–10 €20,400, and Grades 11–12 €23,900. The admissions office can set the instalments out in writing before a place is confirmed.

Refunds

The application fee of €250 is one-time and non-refundable. The enrolment deposit of €2,000 is one-time and is credited to the final term; it is the payment that confirms the place after an offer. Tuition is billed for the school year and may be paid in the August, January and April instalments, or in full by 15 July for 3 percent off. The school does not publish any other refund figure. A family considering a withdrawal should write to admissions@kanade-school.example or call +351 21 000 4800 during office hours, Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 16:30, so the remaining instalments can be explained against that family’s own account. Bus and lunch, where chosen, are the optional annual charges of €1,650 and €1,280.

pages.title: Curriculum
pages.content:
Kanade offers the IB Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma Programmes on one campus. English is the teaching language from Kindergarten to Grade 12.

Primary Years Programme

The Primary Years Programme runs from Kindergarten through Grade 5, for children from the year they turn four up to the end of primary. Teaching is in English. Portuguese starts in Kindergarten, and mother-tongue clubs give room for the languages spoken at home. Tomás Ferreira, Head of Primary, coordinates this part of the school. Classes sit inside a week that begins with arrival at 8:20 and lessons from 8:30 to 15:20. Young children spend time with books, blocks and the library as part of ordinary learning, not as an extra programme. Kindergarten tuition for ages 4–5 is €14,800 for the school year, and Primary Years tuition for Grades 1–5 is €17,600. Both figures are for 2026–27.

Middle Years Programme

The Middle Years Programme is for Grades 6 to 10. Amara Nwosu is MYP Coordinator. Students go on learning in English, continue Portuguese, and add French or German from Grade 6. The Personal Project belongs to Grade 10 and is shown at the Grade 10 Personal Project exhibition. Science learning uses the school laboratories; a new science wing opens in September. Tuition for Middle Years, Grades 6–10, is €20,400 for the 2026–27 school year. The school day is the same as for the rest of the campus: arrival at 8:20, lessons from 8:30 to 15:20, and activities until 16:30. Grade 10 is the last year of MYP before students move into the Diploma Programme.

Diploma Programme

The Diploma Programme is for Grades 11 and 12. Jonas Becker is DP Coordinator. Students work towards the IB Diploma in English, with the library used heavily for the extended essay and for independent study. Priya Raman, DP class of 2025, has written about that essay work and about the library. Tuition for the Diploma Programme, Grades 11–12, is €23,900 for 2026–27, and tuition includes IB exam registration for DP students as well as books and day trips. The programme sits on the same campus as PYP and MYP, so younger and older students share the entrance, the dining hall and the grounds. An offer of a DP place follows the same five admissions steps as every other year group.

Languages

English is the teaching language. Portuguese is taught from Kindergarten. From Grade 6, students take French or German. Mother-tongue clubs support the languages families already speak, which matters in a school of about 40 nationalities. Mei-Lin Chou is Head of Languages and oversees this pathway from the early years through the Diploma Programme. Keeping a home language is part of how the school describes itself: children learn in English, keep the language of home, and leave ready for the IB Diploma. The language teams share the library, where shelves are used for class reading and for quiet study. No separate language fee is charged; language teaching sits inside tuition for the year group.

Arts and sport

Arts and sport run across the campus, from the music room to the outdoor court and the grass field. Students play violin and cello in the music room, and basketball is part of after-school sport on the outdoor court. These are ordinary parts of the week, not a separate academy. On activity afternoons the programme is on the timetable from 14:30, and activities finish by 16:30. Break at 10:40 is time on the field. The lunch hour at 12:30 is in the dining hall for students on the lunch programme. Nothing in arts or sport is billed on top of tuition unless a family chooses the optional lunch programme at €1,280 or the bus at €1,650.

pages.title: Campus life
pages.content:
The school day runs from arrival at 8:20 to activities ending at 16:30. Library, sport, music and lunch sit inside that day.

Library, sport, music and lunch

Four places organise most of the day outside lessons. The library is a bright room where students read in the window light; older students also use it for Diploma study and the extended essay. Sport is on the grass field at break and on the outdoor court after school, including basketball. Music is a working room for violin and cello. Lunch is served in the dining hall at long tables. Break falls at 10:40, lunch at 12:30, and many activities are underway by 15:30. Families see these places on an open morning, Tuesday 10 November 2026, Tuesday 12 January 2027 or Tuesday 9 February 2027, from 9:30 to 11:00. The campus entrance is the low white building under the oak canopy at Rua do Jardim Alto 18.

After-school activities

Lessons run from 8:30 to 15:20. On activity afternoons, clubs and practices are on the timetable from 14:30, and the campus stays open for activities until 16:30. By 15:30 many students are on the outdoor court, in the music room or still in the library. The activities grow out of the school’s own arts and sport, including strings and basketball, rather than from a separate list of outside providers. Arrival in the morning is 8:20. Students who go home at the end of lessons leave after 15:20; students who stay are finished by 16:30, which is also when the office closes. Parents who need the later finish can match it with the bus or with their own pickup at the gate.

The school bus

The school bus is optional and costs €1,650 for the school year. Four routes serve the campus. The stop beside the school is Jardim Alto. Families who use public transport instead can come by Metro and then bus 728 to that stop. The bus charge is not included in tuition and is not covered by the 10 percent reduction for a third and further child. It can be paid with the fee instalments in August, January and April. Morning arrival at school is 8:20, so routes are timed for the gate at that hour. The office can confirm whether a home address sits on one of the four routes. Write to office@kanade-school.example or call +351 21 000 4800.

Lunch

The lunch programme is optional and costs €1,280 for the school year. Students on the programme eat in the dining hall at 12:30. The charge is separate from tuition. Tuition itself includes books, day trips, and IB exam registration for Diploma Programme students, but it does not include lunch or the bus. The 10 percent reduction for a third and further child applies to tuition only, not to lunch. Families who do not take the programme should arrange their own midday meal. Questions about menus and about starting or stopping lunch go to office@kanade-school.example during office hours, Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 16:30. The dining hall is one of the places walked on an open morning.

pages.title: Calendar
pages.content:
The 2026–27 year is three terms, from 1 September 2026 to 25 June 2027. Open mornings, the winter concert and the application deadline sit inside that year.

Term dates for 2026–27

Term 1 runs from 1 September 2026 to 18 December 2026. Term 2 runs from 6 January 2027 to 26 March 2027. Term 3 runs from 12 April 2027 to 25 June 2027. The school is closed between these dates. August and January are the main entry points for new students, so many new families start on 1 September or on 6 January. Priority applications for August 2027 entry close on 31 March 2027. Office hours on school days stay Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 16:30, including through the weeks when an open morning is held. Term dates are the same for Kindergarten, Primary Years, Middle Years and the Diploma Programme.

Dates through the year

Eight dates anchor the year for families and for applicants. Term 1 begins on 1 September 2026. The first open morning is Tuesday 10 November 2026, 9:30 to 11:00. The winter concert is on 17 December 2026, late in Term 1, which ends on 18 December 2026. Term 2 begins on 6 January 2027. The next open morning is Tuesday 12 January 2027, 9:30 to 11:00, and the one after that is Tuesday 9 February 2027, also 9:30 to 11:00. Priority applications for August 2027 entry close on 31 March 2027. Term 3 begins on 12 April 2027 and ends on 25 June 2027. Open mornings are visits, not assessment days.

The school day

The school day has the same hours in every term. Arrival is at 8:20. Lessons run from 8:30 to 15:20. Activities continue until 16:30. Break is at 10:40, lunch is at 12:30, and many after-school activities are underway by 15:30. On activity afternoons the programme is listed from 14:30. Parents report an absence by email by 8:15, before the gate rush at 8:20. The office is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 16:30, so it opens before arrival and closes as activities end. Open mornings sit outside this lesson timetable: they are Tuesdays, 9:30 to 11:00, on 10 November 2026, 12 January 2027 and 9 February 2027.

pages.title: Our people
pages.content:
Seven people lead the school, the programmes and the admissions office. Families meet them by role, starting with the Head of School and the Director of Admissions.

Dr. Helena Marsh, Head of School

Dr. Helena Marsh is Head of School. She is responsible for Kanade International School as a whole: 640 students aged 4 to 18, Kindergarten to Grade 12, from about 40 nationalities, taught in English. The school was founded in 1994 and offers the IB Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma Programmes on the Lisbon campus. Families meet the school at an open morning or on a private tour before they apply.

Leila Haddad, Director of Admissions

Leila Haddad is Director of Admissions. She handles enquiries, open mornings, applications, the assessment and family meeting, and offers. Write to admissions@kanade-school.example or call +351 21 000 4800. The office replies within two school days. A complete application includes previous school reports and the €250 application fee. The enrolment deposit of €2,000 confirms a place and is credited to the final term. Open mornings in this cycle are 10 November 2026, 12 January 2027 and 9 February 2027, all Tuesdays, 9:30 to 11:00.

Tomás Ferreira, Head of Primary

Tomás Ferreira is Head of Primary and leads the Primary Years Programme from Kindergarten through Grade 5. Teaching in these years is in English, with Portuguese from Kindergarten and mother-tongue clubs for languages spoken at home. Kindergarten tuition for ages 4–5 is €14,800 for 2026–27, and Primary Years tuition for Grades 1–5 is €17,600. The primary day uses the same hours as the rest of the school: arrival at 8:20, lessons from 8:30 to 15:20, activities until 16:30. He works with Mei-Lin Chou on the language pathway in the early years.

Amara Nwosu, MYP Coordinator

Amara Nwosu is MYP Coordinator for Grades 6 to 10. From Grade 6, students add French or German beside English and Portuguese. Grade 10 includes the Personal Project, which is presented at the Grade 10 Personal Project exhibition. Middle Years tuition is €20,400 for the 2026–27 school year. Science lessons use the laboratories, and a new science wing opens in September. The MYP years share the library, the music room, the dining hall and the sports spaces with the rest of the campus. Questions about a Grade 6 to 10 place still begin with admissions, not with a separate MYP office.

Jonas Becker, DP Coordinator

Jonas Becker is DP Coordinator for Grades 11 and 12. Diploma students work in English towards the IB Diploma, with IB exam registration included in tuition, alongside books and day trips. Diploma Programme tuition is €23,900 for 2026–27. The library is central to DP study, including the extended essay. Priya Raman, of the DP class of 2025, has described that essay work and the library from a student’s side. DP students follow the same school day as the rest of the campus and the same admissions steps as younger applicants. An offer is confirmed with the €2,000 enrolment deposit.

Mei-Lin Chou, Head of Languages

Mei-Lin Chou is Head of Languages. English is the teaching language of the school. Portuguese is taught from Kindergarten. French or German begins in Grade 6. Mother-tongue clubs support the languages of home in a student body of about 40 nationalities. The language pathway runs through PYP, MYP and DP, so she works with Tomás Ferreira, Amara Nwosu and Jonas Becker rather than inside a single year group. Language classes use the library as well as classrooms. There is no extra fee for the language pathway; it is part of tuition for the child’s year.

Rafael Ortiz, Pastoral and Wellbeing Lead

Rafael Ortiz is Pastoral and Wellbeing Lead for students from Kindergarten to Grade 12. Pastoral care sits alongside the academic programmes and covers the school day from arrival at 8:20 to the close of activities at 16:30. Parents report an absence by email by 8:15 so the morning register is accurate before lessons start at 8:30. He is the named lead families ask for when a question is about a child’s welfare rather than about a place, a fee or a subject. Admissions questions remain with Leila Haddad, and day-to-day office messages go to office@kanade-school.example.

pages.title: Parents
pages.content:
This page is the hub for families already at Kanade. It gathers the month’s dates, the school day, bus and lunch, absence reporting and the written policies.

This month

Three dates are the ones families ask about first. Tuesday 10 November 2026 is an open morning, 9:30 to 11:00, useful if a sibling or a visiting relative needs to see the campus. The winter concert is on 17 December 2026, near the end of Term 1, which closes on 18 December 2026. Term 2 begins on 6 January 2027. Later open mornings, if you are planning ahead, are Tuesday 12 January 2027 and Tuesday 9 February 2027, both 9:30 to 11:00. Priority applications for August 2027 entry close on 31 March 2027. None of these dates changes the daily hours: arrival 8:20, lessons 8:30 to 15:20, activities until 16:30.

Calendar, bus and lunch, and policies

The parent hub points to three places you will use again. The calendar holds term dates and the eight named events for 2026–27. Bus and lunch covers the optional bus at €1,650 a year on four routes, and the optional lunch programme at €1,280 a year. Policies covers the written statements the school publishes for families, including privacy and safeguarding, together with the absence rule below. Tuition, the application fee and the enrolment deposit are set out on the fees page, not in this hub. For a missed morning, email the office by 8:15 at office@kanade-school.example. The office phone is +351 21 000 4800, and office hours are Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 16:30.

The school day

Arrival is at 8:20, through the campus gate and along the tree-lined path. Lessons run from 8:30 to 15:20. Break is at 10:40, lunch is at 12:30 in the dining hall for students on the lunch programme, and activities run on until 16:30. On activity afternoons the programme starts from 14:30, and by 15:30 students are often on the court, in music or in the library. The office opens at 8:00, before the gate, and closes at 16:30. These hours are the same in Term 1, Term 2 and Term 3. A child leaving at the end of lessons is collected after 15:20. A child who stays for activities is collected by 16:30.

Bus, lunch and absence

The bus is optional, €1,650 for the year, on four routes, with the school stop at Jardim Alto. Lunch is optional, €1,280 for the year, served at 12:30. Neither charge is inside tuition, and neither receives the 10 percent sibling reduction. If your child will be absent, email office@kanade-school.example by 8:15, before arrival at 8:20. Give the child’s name and year group. A later message can still be sent, but 8:15 is the time that reaches the office before the register. The same address handles bus route questions and lunch. Admissions for a sibling is a different inbox: admissions@kanade-school.example, with a reply within two school days.

Policies

Current families use the privacy statement and the safeguarding statement as the two written policies published with the site. Privacy covers how the school uses the details you send to admissions, to the office and to careers. Safeguarding names Rafael Ortiz, Pastoral and Wellbeing Lead, as the person responsible for student welfare during the school day. Absence reporting by 8:15 sits with those expectations. Fee rules that affect a family mid-year are also written down: the application fee is non-refundable, the enrolment deposit is credited to the final term, instalments fall in August, January and April, and full payment by 15 July receives 3 percent off. The office will send the statement that matches your question.

pages.title: Careers
pages.content:
Kanade is hiring for three roles in the Middle Years, the Primary Years and learning support. Send a CV to the careers address before the closing date on the role.

Why teach at Kanade

Kanade International School was founded in 1994 and is an IB World School offering the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma Programmes. Teaching is in English. About 640 students, aged 4 to 18, come from about 40 nationalities and learn on one campus in Lisbon, at Rua do Jardim Alto 18, 1400-150 Lisboa. A teacher here works with colleagues across the three programmes rather than in a separate school for each age.

The language pathway is part of every week. Portuguese begins in Kindergarten, French or German begins in Grade 6, and mother-tongue clubs sit beside English-medium lessons. Mei-Lin Chou leads that work. Class teachers and specialists plan next to the people who hold the programme roles: Tomás Ferreira in primary, Amara Nwosu in the Middle Years and Jonas Becker in the Diploma.

The school day is bounded and publishable. Students arrive at 8:20, lessons run from 8:30 to 15:20, and activities continue until 16:30. Staff collaborate in a shared staff room. Pastoral questions go to Rafael Ortiz. The Head of School is Dr. Helena Marsh.

Open positions

Three roles are open. The closing date is the date on each role.

MYP Mathematics teacher. The post is in the Middle Years Programme, Grades 6 to 10, and closes on 30 November 2026.

PYP Grade 3 homeroom teacher. The post is in the Primary Years Programme and closes on 15 January 2027.

Learning support specialist. The post works with students across the school and closes on 31 January 2027.

Each closing date is final for that advertisement. Later open mornings for families, on 12 January 2027 and 9 February 2027, are not interview days. The campus is at Rua do Jardim Alto 18, 1400-150 Lisboa.

How to apply

Send a CV by email to careers@kanade-school.example. Use the role title in the subject line: MYP Mathematics teacher, PYP Grade 3 homeroom teacher, or Learning support specialist. The message should name the closing date you are applying against, 30 November 2026, 15 January 2027 or 31 January 2027. The careers address is only for applications. Families asking about a school place should write to admissions@kanade-school.example, and other office matters go to office@kanade-school.example. The phone is +351 21 000 4800, and office hours are Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 16:30. There is no online form. A CV attached to that email is the application.

pages.title: Stories and news
pages.content:
Three family stories and three news posts sit on this page. The stories follow the Andersen family, Priya Raman and the Silva Okoro family.

The Andersen family

The Andersen family moved from Copenhagen in 2024. Their children are in Grade 2 and Grade 7, so one child is in the Primary Years Programme and the other is in the Middle Years Programme. They write about settling in within the first term: the 8:20 arrival, the first weeks in English-medium classes, and keeping a home language while Portuguese is taught from Kindergarten and, for the older child, a new language is on the Grade 6 pathway. The family story is the long read on this site. It stays with that first term and does not report later results. Both children joined a school of 640 students from about 40 nationalities, founded in 1994, on the Lisbon campus.

Priya Raman

Priya Raman is in the Diploma Programme class of 2025. Her piece is about the extended essay and the library: where she sat to work, how the carrels are used, and what it was like to research inside an English-medium DP cohort. Jonas Becker is DP Coordinator for Grades 11 and 12. The essay is part of the Diploma, and IB exam registration for DP students is included in tuition, which for Grades 11–12 is €23,900 in 2026–27. Priya’s account is a student’s view of work already completed in the class of 2025. It is not a promise about later classes. The library she describes is the same room younger students use for ordinary reading.

The Silva Okoro family

The Silva Okoro family is a Portuguese-Nigerian family and joined in January, one of the two main entry points. They write about keeping two home languages while their children learn in English. That account sits beside the school’s language pathway: English as the teaching language, Portuguese from Kindergarten, French or German from Grade 6, and mother-tongue clubs. Mei-Lin Chou, Head of Languages, leads that pathway. January entry follows the same five admissions steps as August entry, including previous school reports, the €250 application fee and, after an offer, the €2,000 enrolment deposit. Their story is about language at home in the first months, not about a particular class or teacher.

New science wing opens in September

A new science wing opens in September, at the start of the school year. Term 1 begins on 1 September 2026. The wing is for science lessons, including the practical work Middle Years students already do at the lab benches. It is part of the same campus, at Rua do Jardim Alto 18, 1400-150 Lisboa, and it does not change the school day: arrival at 8:20, lessons from 8:30 to 15:20, activities until 16:30. Amara Nwosu, MYP Coordinator, oversees Grades 6 to 10, where that laboratory work sits in the programme. No separate fee is charged for use of the wing. Middle Years tuition remains €20,400 for 2026–27.

Grade 10 Personal Project exhibition

Grade 10 students in the Middle Years Programme show their Personal Projects at the exhibition. The Personal Project is part of MYP, which Amara Nwosu coordinates for Grades 6 to 10. Families of Grade 10 students are invited to see the work. The exhibition is a school event on the campus, not an external fair. It does not replace term dates or the winter concert on 17 December 2026. Projects are completed in English, the teaching language, with the library available for research in the same way DP students use it for the extended essay. Tuition for these grades is €20,400 for the 2026–27 school year, and the exhibition has no separate ticket charge in the fee list.

Winter concert programme

The winter concert is on 17 December 2026. The programme post sets out the order of the evening for families. Music at Kanade includes strings, and students play violin and cello in the music room during the year; the concert is the evening those ensembles play for parents. Term 1 ends the next day, on 18 December 2026, and Term 2 does not begin until 6 January 2027. The concert is on campus. It is not an open morning: the visits for prospective families remain 10 November 2026, 12 January 2027 and 9 February 2027, Tuesdays, 9:30 to 11:00. Office hours on the day of the concert still follow the published Monday to Friday pattern, 8:00 to 16:30, unless the office writes to parents with a change.

pages.title: Contact and visit
pages.content:
The campus is at Rua do Jardim Alto 18, 1400-150 Lisboa. The office is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 16:30, and open mornings are on three published Tuesdays.

Address and office hours

Kanade International School is at Rua do Jardim Alto 18, 1400-150 Lisboa, Portugal. The office is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 16:30. The phone is +351 21 000 4800. Three email addresses cover the work of the office. Admissions is admissions@kanade-school.example. The general office is office@kanade-school.example. Careers is careers@kanade-school.example. There is no enquiry form on this page. Use the phone during office hours, or send email to the address that matches the question. A new admissions enquiry receives a reply within two school days. The campus entrance is the low white building, with oak canopy and trees along the path.

Getting here

The school stop is Jardim Alto. Come by Metro and then take bus 728 to Jardim Alto. The campus gate opens onto a tree-lined path used each morning at 8:20. Families visiting for an open morning should arrive for a 9:30 start and plan to finish at 11:00. The visit dates are Tuesday 10 November 2026, Tuesday 12 January 2027 and Tuesday 9 February 2027. A private tour can be booked through admissions when those mornings do not work. The optional school bus, for enrolled students, uses four routes and costs €1,650 for the year; it is not a public bus, and bus 728 is the public route to the stop. Drivers can set the address as Rua do Jardim Alto 18, 1400-150 Lisboa.

Book an open morning

To book an open morning, email admissions@kanade-school.example or call +351 21 000 4800 and ask for Leila Haddad, Director of Admissions. Say which Tuesday you want: 10 November 2026, 12 January 2027 or 9 February 2027. The visit runs from 9:30 to 11:00. If you are writing about a place for a child aged 4 to 18, include the year group you have in mind and whether you are aiming for August or January entry. To confirm a job application, use careers@kanade-school.example instead and attach a CV. For absence, bus and lunch, use office@kanade-school.example. The office is staffed Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 16:30, at Rua do Jardim Alto 18.

pages.title: Privacy
pages.content:
This statement describes what Kanade holds about families and applicants, and which address receives which kind of message. It is the privacy text for the school.

What the school holds

Kanade International School, at Rua do Jardim Alto 18, 1400-150 Lisboa, Portugal, holds the details families send so that a child can be considered for a place, enrolled, and looked after during the school day. That includes the name of the child and the family, the year group, previous school reports sent with an application, and the email address and phone number you use with us. The application fee of €250 and the enrolment deposit of €2,000 are recorded against the application and the offer. Fee charges for 2026–27, including tuition by year group and the optional bus and lunch, are held on the family account. The school was founded in 1994 and teaches about 640 students aged 4 to 18.

Who receives your message

Email is read by the office it is sent to. admissions@kanade-school.example is for places, visits and applications, and a new enquiry is answered within two school days. office@kanade-school.example is for absence, the bus and lunch. Absence messages should arrive by 8:15. careers@kanade-school.example is for a CV and a role application, and is not used for student places. The phone +351 21 000 4800 is answered during office hours, Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 16:30. Please do not send a CV to the admissions address or a child’s reports to the careers address. Each inbox is limited to that work. The campus address above is the place to write to if you need a postal reply.

Asking about your own details

A parent or guardian may ask what is held about their own child, or ask for a correction, by emailing office@kanade-school.example or calling +351 21 000 4800 during Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 16:30. Staff applications are handled only through careers@kanade-school.example. The school does not sell family details. Details are used to reply to you, to run admissions, to administer fees and the optional bus and lunch, and to look after students during the published day, from arrival at 8:20 until activities end at 16:30. This page does not set a retention period in years, and it does not name any outside processor. If a question is about safeguarding rather than about data, write to the office and it will be passed to Rafael Ortiz, Pastoral and Wellbeing Lead.

pages.title: Safeguarding
pages.content:
Rafael Ortiz, Pastoral and Wellbeing Lead, is the person responsible for safeguarding concerns. Contact the school office during Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 16:30.

Who is responsible

Rafael Ortiz is Pastoral and Wellbeing Lead at Kanade International School and is the person responsible for safeguarding concerns about students. The school educates 640 students aged 4 to 18, from Kindergarten to Grade 12, at Rua do Jardim Alto 18, 1400-150 Lisboa. Dr. Helena Marsh is Head of School. A concern about a child’s welfare should go to Rafael Ortiz through the school office, not through the admissions inbox and not through careers. Email office@kanade-school.example or call +351 21 000 4800. Office hours are Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 16:30. If the concern is about an absence that morning, the 8:15 email still applies, and a welfare worry can be written in the same message.

During the school day

Students are on campus for a published day. Arrival is at 8:20, lessons run from 8:30 to 15:20, and activities continue until 16:30. On activity afternoons the programme is timetable from 14:30. Parents report an absence by email by 8:15 so staff know who is expected before the gate. The office opens at 8:00 and closes at 16:30. Break at 10:40, lunch at 12:30 and the later activities are part of the supervised day for students who are present. The optional bus, on four routes, is for enrolled students travelling to and from this day. Visitors, including families on an open morning from 9:30 to 11:00, stay with the member of staff who is hosting them.

How to raise a concern

Email office@kanade-school.example with the subject line Safeguarding, or call +351 21 000 4800 and ask for Rafael Ortiz, Pastoral and Wellbeing Lead. Say the student’s name, year group and what you are worried about. The office is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 16:30. Admissions questions, including applications and open mornings, stay with Leila Haddad at admissions@kanade-school.example. Job applications stay with careers@kanade-school.example. This statement does not publish a separate emergency number, and it does not describe a sanction ladder. It names the lead, the hours, and the address to use. A parent who needs the privacy statement as well will find it as its own page. Both statements are text only and can be read before a visit.
